subject: Private CP identity concierge: assertion enrichment + SCIM patch behavior

Subject: Private CP onboarding — assertion enrichment question

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the quick demo earlier. We're starting the control-plane connect runbook and ran into a question around SAML assertions and SCIM upstream behavior for your private control plane deployment. Two specifics: 

1) We need to include an "operator_id" claim in the SAML assertion for operator-level actions (provisioning / break-glass) — is Redwood able to accept custom attributes and map them to role bindings?

2) SCIM: when we sync group membership we sometimes send PATCH operations with "Operations": [{"op": "add", "path": "members", "value": [...] }] — does the private control plane apply patch semantics atomically or as a best-effort merge? We need deterministic reconciliation for our IAM source of truth.

Attaching a short sample SCIM payload and a proposal for a minimal assertion mapping. Can you loop in the right folks for operator provisioning and audit guarantees?

Appreciate it,
Evelyn
Integrations Lead, Acme Corp

Attachments:
- idp-assertion-enrichment-proposal.pdf
- scim-patch-examples.json

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Acme Integrations <integrations@acme.example.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-18T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private CP onboarding — assertion enrichment question

Evelyn — thanks, this is exactly the right level of detail. Looping in Jordan (priv-deploy) and Naomi (security/compliance) to confirm mapping and SCIM semantics. Quick answers up front:

- Custom SAML attributes: yes — we can accept and map custom attributes. There are two supported flows:
  * Attribute-to-role mapping: map an assertion attribute (e.g., operator_id or operator_role) to an internal role claim; suitable for immediate routing and RBAC enforcement.
  * Assertion enrichment: treat attributes as metadata stored against the authentication event for audit and policy decisions (e.g., break-glass).

- SCIM PATCH semantics: our private control plane supports full-transaction application when run against the primary provisioning service in the customer's VPC. If a connector is configured in a fan-out mode (multiple downstream targets) we provide best-effort merge semantics and a reconciliation loop.

We'll propose a small recommended configuration and a fallback: if you require atomic SCIM patches for membership we recommend:
  1) Use a single authoritative SCIM endpoint (no fan-out).
  2) Enable explicit reconciliation window (we support 30s–5m).
  3) Configure the connector to reject conflicting patches with a 409 so you can gate via your provisioning pipeline.

Jordan/Naomi — can you review the attached proposal and confirm operator service-account rotation & audit retention expectations?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Product Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, Acme Integrations <integrations@acme.example.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-18T13:24:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private CP onboarding — assertion enrichment question

Thanks Vanessa. A few operational clarifications from the deployment side: 

- Operator identity: we recommend mapping operator_id -> subject.external_id and operator_role -> internal.role. For privileged operator sessions we create a short-lived operator token bound to the SAML assertion and to a hardware-backed KMS key (customer-managed if requested). Rotation: default 7 days; we can shorten to 24h for high-risk customers.

- Break-glass pattern: we support a "break-glass" service account that can be provisioned as a one-off via SCIM create (not via PATCH). We log the event, require MFA, and persist the SAML assertion with the audit record for 365 days by default (configurable).

- SCIM semantics: our SCIM adapter supports both PATCH and full PUT. When you choose PATCH-atomic mode we run the operation inside a database transaction; this is only available when the connector is configured in single-writer mode (no downstream replication). If you enable multi-target fan-out, we switch to eventual merge and emit a reconciliation event stream (Kafka) that you can consume.

Attached: small note on operator service account rotation and the default audit retention. Ben — can you confirm there are no infra blockers for the KMS-bound tokens in Acme's region?

-Jordan

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, Acme Integrations <integrations@acme.example.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-19T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private CP onboarding — assertion enrichment question

Jordan/Evelyn — quick infra check: Acme's requested region (us-west-2) supports our KMS integration and HSM-backed envelope keys with no additional network peering requirements beyond the VPC egress to the KMS endpoint. Two notes:

- If Acme wants customer-managed KMS (BYOK) we'll need the key ARN and an IAM principal to grant Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey permissions.
- For audit exports: we can stream to a customer-controlled S3 bucket (VPC endpoint recommended) or push to an on-prem collector over a TLS mutual-auth channel.

No blockers on our side; we can include these steps in the mutual action plan.

-Ben Carter
Infra PM, Redwood Dedicated & Private

Thanks everyone — this is super helpful and clears up the majority of our questions. A couple follow-ups before we finalize the MAT: 

- We will opt for single-writer SCIM + PATCH-atomic mode. Please include the connector config snippet and the 409 gating behavior in the runbook.
- For BYOK: we'll share the key ARN and a service principal next week. Please confirm the minimal IAM permissions again so our security team can pre-authorize.
- Audit retention: can you confirm a configurable upper-bound? We may need 7 years for compliance — is that supported via export?

If you can drop the SCIM connector snippet and the operator token rotation section into the shared Drive folder (link below) we'll mark the ticket ready for provisioning.

—Evelyn
